title: [4/9/2024] Percentages of tourists who used different types of transport
prompt: The graph below shows the percentages of tourists who used different types of transport to travel within a particular nation between 1989 and 2009. Each tourist may have used more than one type of transport. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the percentages of tourists using five different modes of transportation within a country over a 20-year period, from 1989 to 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, with the exception of air travel, all other modes of transport recorded an upward trend during the period shown. Additionally, car and rail were consistently the two most popular choices among tourists, with their usage percentages significantly higher than other means of transport.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the two main modes of transport, cars were initially the most common choice, used by approximately 47% of tourists in 1989, about 12% higher than rail travel. Car usage then rose steadily to peak at 62% in 1999 before declining to roughly 52% by 2009. Meanwhile, rail travel showed consistent growth over the entire period, starting at 35% and eventually overtaking car travel to reach 58% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding other forms of transport, in 1989, air travel was the second most popular option at 39%, while coach and ferry services were used by only 9% and 5% of tourists respectively. Air travel then experienced a continuous decline over the next two decades, falling to 21% by 2009. In contrast, coach travel increased steadily to reach approximately 25% by the end of the period, while ferry usage showed minimal change, ending at roughly 9%.
